chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who faints during the day and then regains consciousness before sunset. He said: He should perform ẓuhr or ʿaṣr. And during the night, if he regains consciousness before dawn, he should make up the night prayer.

So this report accords with what we have stated earlier: that it is obligatory upon him to make up the prayer whose time he regains consciousness within. And this time is the end of the time allotted to the constrained person; thus making it up becomes obligatory at that point.

key_terms.الْمُضْطَرِّ: the constrained person whose prayer time extends to a later limit due to necessity
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer referred to in the report
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, marking the end of the daytime prayer window mentioned here
key_terms.قَضَاءَ: performance as make-up of an owed act after incapacity or missed performance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayers for a person who regains consciousness before sunset or before dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one who was unconscious and then regains consciousness before the end of a prayer's time. It establishes that he must perform or make up the prayer whose time he has reached before its final limit. The report is used in jurisprudence to define the obligation of salat for the unconscious person upon recovery.
